newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria VAE upbeat on 1997 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Austria VAE upbeat on 1997 prospects.

text.p: Austrian points maker VAE AG, reporting a rise in 1996 pre-tax profit but lower net, said on Thursday it was confident of achieving higher earnings and sales this year and flagged new ventures in Europe and Asia.

VAE group pre-tax profit rose to 145.6 million schillings last year from 128.1 million. Net profit, burdened by heavier tax payments, slipped to 111.1 million schillings from 119.9 while earnings per share fell to 71 schillings from 81.
The firm said it planned to pay an unchanged 32 schillings dividend.

Chief executive Edmund Auli told a news conference a healthy order backlog at the start of the year pointed to at least a five percent rise in parent and group sales this year, excluding acquisitions.

VAE's outstanding orders at the end of February were worth 1.4 billion schillings, up from one billion the previous year. Incoming orders in the first two months rose to 876 million schillings from 500 million.
"Our aim over the next two years is to get back to earnings per share of around 80 schillings," VAE financial director Mohamed Kaddoura said.
The firm saw investments steady at around 120 million schillings in 1997.
Auli forecast the launch of two new joint ventures in Eastern Europe in the first half and said he was also optimistic long-running talks on two Chinese joint ventures would yield an agreement.
He added that the firm was planning a capital increase at its U.S. subsidiary and expansion in Australia.
VAE said all of its units finished 1996 comfortably in the black. Outside Austria, the firm has interests in Austria, the Baltic states, Hungary, Spain and Britain.
VAE shares closed 12 schillings up at 1,165 in an otherwise limp Vienna market. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
